body.statement:
Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be mutually absolutely continuous laws on one observed-data space, and suppose their target values are \(+a\) and \(-a\), where \(a>0\).  Write \(P_{+1}:=P_+\) and \(P_{-1}:=P_-\).  Then every measurable estimator \(\widehat\vartheta\) satisfies
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_{P_v}[(\widehat\vartheta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Put \(A=\int\sqrt{dP_+dP_-}\) and \(O=\int\min(dP_+,dP_-)\).  Mutual absolute continuity makes the likelihood ratio finite almost surely.  Jensen's inequality under \(P_+\) gives
\[
 A=E_{P_+}\!\left[\exp\!\left\{-\frac12\log\frac{dP_+}{dP_-}\right\}\right]
 \ge\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)/2\}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(A^2\le O(2-O)\le2O\), so
\[
 O\ge\frac12\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}.
\]
Classify an arbitrary estimator as plus when \(\widehat\vartheta\ge0\).  On every classification error the squared distance from the corresponding target \(\pm a\) is at least \(a^2\).  Pointwise in the two densities, every binary rule pays the smaller density, so the sum of its two error probabilities is at least \(O\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_{P_v}[(\widehat\vartheta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2O}{2}
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\},
\]
as claimed.
body.justification: This isolates the exact two-point squared-error reduction used by both components of the minimax converse.
body.gap: The reduction is elementary but must be a declared node because both lower-bound arguments invoke it.
body.consumer: It converts the parametric and signed-depth divergence bounds into minimax risk lower bounds.
